headline: The incident at the BioUrja ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois remains very active this morning. Peoria Police Chief Brad Dixon said at an overnight press conference that one device has been rendered safe, but the rest of the facility has not been cleared and the search will continue throughout much of today. Chief Dixon confirmed that a device was found Friday afternoon after the plant reported a bomb threat. Chief Dixon reiterated that the threat is credible and the incident is still active. He would not confirm whether more than one device has been located. The FBI and ATF are on scene assisting Peoria authorities. A one mile evacuation zone around the plant on Edmund Street remains in effect across parts of Peoria and East Peoria, with more than 5,000 people reportedly evacuated. About 75 people are sheltering at Manual Academy. The next scheduled update is at noon. The timeline of events as relayed by the Chief: 1:08p.m - BioUrja contacted Peoria Police in reference to a bomb threat 2:00p.m. (approximately) - A suspicious device was located and additional resources requested to the scene 6:45p.m. - Device determined to be credible and a 1 mile blast radius was established 7:02p.m - Mass notification ordering evacuation within the 1 mile blast radius sent 9:12p.m. - Device rendered safe

headline: At a White House press conference, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said officials have “seen zero evidence” that today’s nationwide ground stop was caused by a cyber attack, adding that nothing can be ruled out. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the problem began at 3:36 p.m. ET, when the FAA began seeing inconsistent radar and communications data because network equipment became overloaded. He said the old hardware went down and that none of the new systems failed. Sites that had been upgraded to new IP based switches stayed online, he said. Secretary Duffy used the outage to renew his call for Congress to fund an overhaul of the air traffic control system, increasing his ask from $30 billion to $50 billion.

headline: Russia's Abu Dhabi wish list reached far past Ukraine, German diplomats told Bild. Moscow would keep occupied Ukrainian land and take all of Donbas. Finland would exit NATO. headline: Microsoft says there is still no "sustained recovery" from a global outage now more than 12 hours old. Earlier, the company had pointed to "positive results" in its repair efforts. Outlook, Teams and other office staples remain unavailable to millions. Banks, governments and courts in multiple countries are affected. Downdetector logged reports from 74 countries and territories within about an hour. City governments across the U.S. reported widespread email problems. In Hong Kong, Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs bankers told CNN their work was disrupted. Microsoft: The outage was not caused by a cybersecurity breach.
